source_text: Τοιούτοις οὖν ὑποδείγμασιν κολληθῆναι καὶ ἡμᾶς δεῖ, ἀδελφοί. γέγραπται γάρ: Κολλᾶσθε τοῖς ἁγίοις, ὅτι οἱ κολλώμενοι αὐτοῖς ἁγιασθήσονται. καὶ πάλιν ἐν ἑτέρῳ τόπῳ λέγει: Μετὰ ἀνδρὸς ἀθῷον ἀθῷος ἔσῃ καὶ μετὰ ἐκλεκτοῦ ἐκλεκτὸς ἔσῃ. καὶ μετὰ στρεβλοῦ διαστρέψεις. κολληθῶμεν οὖν τοῖς ἀθῴοις καὶ δικαίοις: εἰσὶν δὲ οὗτοι ἐκλεκτοὶ τοῦ θεοῦ. ἱνατί ἔρεις καὶ θυμοὶ καὶ διχοστασίαι καὶ σχίσματα πόλεμός τε ἐν ὑμῖν; ἢ οὐχὶ ἕνα θεὸν ἔχομεν καὶ ἔνα Χριστὸν καὶ ἓν πνεῦμα τῆς χάριτος τὸ ἐκχυθὲν ἐφ̓ ἡμᾶς; καὶ μία κλῆσις ἐν Χριστῷ; ἱνατί διέλκομεν καὶ διασπῶμεν τὰ μέλη τοῦ Χριστοῦ καὶ στασιάζομεν πρὸς τὸ σῶμα τὸ ἴδιον, καὶ εἰς τοσαύτην ἀπόνοιαν ἐρχόμεθα, ὥστε ἐπιλαθέσθαι ἡμᾶς, ὅτι μέλη ἐσμὲν ἀλλήλων; μνήσθητε τῶν λόγων τοῦ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ. εἶπεν γάρ: Οὐαὶ τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ ἐκείνῳ: καλὸν ἦν αὐτῷ, εἰ οὐκ ἐγεννήθη, ἦ ἕνα τῶν ἐκλεκτῶν μου σκανδαλίσαι κρεῖττον ἢν αὐτῷ περιτεθῆναι μύλον καὶ καταπον τισθῆναι εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν, ἢ ἕνα τῶν ἐκλεκτῶν μου διαστρέψαι. τὸ σχίσμα ὑμῶν πολλοὺς διέστρεψεν, πολλοὺς εἰς ἀθυμίαν ἔβαλεν, πολλοὺς: εἰς δισταγμόν, τοὺς πάντας ἡμᾶς εἰς λύπην: καὶ ἐπίμονος ἀμῶν ἐστιν ἡ στάσις.
pass_a_gloss: We ought to cling to such examples, brothers. For it is written: Cling to the holy ones, because those who cling to them will be sanctified. And again in another place it says: With an innocent man you will be innocent, and with an elect man you will be elect, and with a crooked man you will be perverted. Let us cling therefore to the innocent and righteous: for these are the elect of God. Why are there strife and anger and divisions and schisms and war among you? Do we not have one God and one Christ and one Spirit of grace that has been poured out upon us? And one calling in Christ? Why do we tear apart and divide the members of Christ and rebel against our own body, and come to such a state of mindlessness that we forget that we are members of one another? Remember the words of the Lord Jesus. For he said: Woe to that man: it would have been good for him if he had not been born, or if one of my elect had been scandalized, it would be better for him to have a millstone put around his neck and to be thrown into the sea, or to pervert one of my elect. Your schism has perverted many, has thrown many into despair, has thrown many into doubt, has thrown all of us into grief: and your rebellion is a persistent affliction.
pass_b_english: Brothers, we must cling to examples like these. Scripture says, "Cling to the holy ones, because those who cling to them will be sanctified." In another place it says, "With an innocent person you will be innocent, and with an elect person you will be elect, but with a crooked person you will be twisted." So let us cling to the innocent and righteous, for these are God's elect. Why do strife, anger, divisions, schisms, and war exist among you? Do we not have one God, one Christ, and one Spirit of grace poured out upon us? And one calling in Christ? Why do we tear apart and scatter the members of Christ and rebel against our own body? Why have we sunk into such mindlessness that we forget we are members of one another? Remember the words of the Lord Jesus. He said, "Woe to that person. It would have been better for them not to have been born than to scandalize one of my elect. It would be better to have a millstone hung around their neck and be thrown into the sea than to pervert one of my elect." Your schism has perverted many, driven many to despair, thrown many into doubt, and brought grief to all of us. Your rebellion is a persistent affliction.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Greek text. Pass A and Pass B are consistent with the source. Scripture allusions (the 'millstone' and 'innocent man' motifs) are correctly rendered. The translation of 'ἐπίμονος ἀμῶν ἐστιν ἡ στάσις' as 'your rebellion is a persistent affliction' (Pass A) and 'Your rebellion is a persistent affliction' (Pass B) correctly interprets the sense of the Greek regarding the ongoing state of faction/rebellion.
